'''''Rogiera''''' is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Rubiaceae]]. It has 15 [[species]] and its native range is from Mexico to Colombia.<ref name="POWO"/>

''[[Rogiera amoena]]'', ''Rogiera cordata'', and ''Rogiera gratissima'' are sometimes [[Gardening|cultivated]] as [[Ornamental plant|ornamentals]].<ref name=rhs>Anthony J. Huxley, Mark Griffiths, and Margot Levy (editors). 1992. ''The New Royal Horticultural Society Dictionary of Gardening.'' The Macmillan Press Limited, London; The Stockton Press, New York. {{ISBN|978-0-333-47494-5}} (set)</ref> The [[type species]] for the genus is ''Rogiera amoena''.<ref>''Rogiera'' In: Index Nominum Genericorum. In: [[Regnum Vegetabile]]</ref>

''Rogiera'' was [[Botanical name|named]] and published by [[Jules Émile Planchon]] in ''Flore des Serres et des Jardins de l'Europe'' (Fl. Serres Jard. Eur.) Vol.5 on page 442 in 1849.<ref name="planchon1849">Jules Émile Planchon. 1849. ''Flore des Serres et des Jardins de l'Europe'' 5:442 and illustration.</ref> The name honours the [[Belgians|Belgian]] [[politician]] [[Charles Latour Rogier]] (1800–1885), who was also Minister for the Interior and patron of horticulture.<ref>[[Thomas Moore (botanist)|Thomas Moore]] {{google books|dIgVAwAAQBAJ|The Treasury of Botany, Part 1 (1866)|page=988}}</ref>

Some authors have included ''Rogiera'' in a [[sensu lato|broadly defined]] ''[[Rondeletia (plant)|Rondeletia]]'', but [[molecular phylogenetic]] [[Research|studies]] have shown that ''Rogiera'' is [[Phylogenetic tree|closer]] to ''[[Guettarda]]'' than to ''Rondeletia''.<ref name="manns2010">Ulrika Manns and Birgitta Bremer. 2010. "Towards a better understanding of intertribal relationships and stable tribal delimitations within Cinchonoideae s.s. (Rubiaceae)". ''Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution'' '''56'''(1):21-39. {{doi|10.1016/j.ympev.2010.04.002}}</ref>
